newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products surge on Iraq moves.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products surge on Iraq moves.

text.p: Med oil productsprices surged as crude futures jumped following the Iraqi incursion into its northern Kurdish region, traders said.
Gasoline prices jumped on the back of the strong futures, but traders said the market was still looking generally long despite recent run cuts by refiners.
"The run cuts have helped a little but the market is still generally long and looks like staying that way for a while," a trader said, adding that Italy in particular was well supplied.
Naphtha was also sharply higher with crude and despite improving liquidity, prices were well supported by good demand.
Egyptian product was seen available and more Skikda barrels are seen emerging around the end of the month.
Gas oil premiums were steady with demand from Greece, Spain and a number of French refiners giving support.
A Sept 10-12 Russian cargo, offered last week at quotes cif high +$2.50 basis Genoa, was heard offered at cif high +$3.75. A number of traders said premiums were closer to +$2.00/+$2.50.
A French refiner was seen looking for heating oil and offering quotes cif high +$2.0 basis Lavera, but traders said it was not very keen on current offered premiums.
Fuel oil was firm. Demand was seen to cover the latest tender from Portugal and one Italian refiner said he saw prices at a $1 a tonne premium to the quoted fob high.
Most cargoes in the the tender were won by a single trader, although a French refiner was also thought to have been awarded at least one optional cargo.
An Italian refiner on Friday sold a 25,000 tonne cargo for mid-September to a French refiner, at $1.25 over the high of fob quotes. The refiner holds 1-2 more cargoes in September.
Low sulphur prices were stronger, too, with swaps gaining around $4 or $5 a tonne.
